description: Lists, without running them, the launcher commands op_open_path would try in order
comment: The read-only pair of op_open_path: nothing is started, so the result is stable enough to assert in CI on a headless runner

description: Writes a piece of text or binary content out to a file and opens it with the program the desktop is configured to use
comment: op_write_file plus op_open_path in one call: it returns the path it wrote, so a launcher that cannot start is reported as an error carrying that path instead of a lost false; it does not wait for the program to exit, and the BLOB signatures write the bytes exactly as they are
example: SELECT op_open_content(logo_blob, 'png'); SELECT op_open_content(read_text('report.html'), 'html'); SELECT op_open_content(svg, 'svg', {'dir':'./out', 'part':'sales'})

description: Writes an HTML string to a temporary file and opens it in the system default browser, returning the file path
comment: The zero-configuration shortcut: op_open_content(content, 'html') with every option left at its default (system temp directory, generated name); needs no configuration because SQL renders HTML

description: Opens a local path or URL with the program the desktop is configured to use
comment: true once a launcher has been started, false when none could be started; NULL input short-circuits to NULL and starts nothing

description: Opens a local path or URL and returns as soon as the launcher is started
comment: The non-blocking pair of op_open_path: true means a process was started, not that the target opened

description: Prints a piece of text straight to stdout, bypassing the result set's column formatting
comment: For character art and other line-aligned output the CLI would otherwise wrap: the text is written to stdout as it is and handed back unchanged, so the call can stay in a projection; the optional second argument is what follows the text instead of the default newline
example: SELECT op_print(report, chr(10) || chr(10)); SELECT op_print(tp_qr('https://query.farm')); SELECT op_print('rows: ' || count(*)) FROM t

description: Rewrites a string into something usable as a file name, following sanitize-filename
comment: The crate's own defaults: the illegal characters are deleted (pass a replacement to see where they were), the 255-byte cut is applied, and the Windows rules are on because a query should answer the same way on every machine

description: Tells whether a string is already usable as a file name, rewriting nothing
comment: The predicate half of sanitize-filename: true means op_sanitize_filename with the same options would answer with the value it was given
example: SELECT count(*) FROM files WHERE NOT op_sanitize_filename_check(name)

description: Writes a piece of text or binary content out to a file and returns its path, with the extension required and the directory, file name and name segment optional
comment: Starts nothing: hand the returned path to op_open_path to open it. `dir` defaults to the system temp directory (created when missing), `name` defaults to a generated open-<time>-<part>-<random> name (an explicit name overwrites), and all three options are sanitized as file names; the BLOB signatures write the bytes exactly as they are
example: SELECT op_write_file(read_blob('logo.png'), 'png'); SELECT op_write_file('{"a":1}', 'json'); SELECT op_write_file(svg, 'svg', {'dir':'./out', 'part':'sales'})
